Reading

THE IDENTIFIER TRANSMITS. Card 2 prints the AXN with its glyph carried through the composition layer — the SPXI question of whether an emoji-bearing identifier survives machine composition, answered affirmatively in a citation snippet. The glyph is TRUNCATED to two characters rather than six, so the surface carries the identifier but not the full checksum. Deposit #1068 is THE OBELUS AND THE TOMBSTONE — one of the 31 deposits the registry held with NO BODY FILE until this session recovered it from the account export. The layer was citing a work the archive could not itself serve.

Machine text, verbatim
The Alexanarch Identifier (AXN) is a content-derived identifier used by Alexanarch, a sovereign, self-governing library for machine-mediated scholarship. Designed to bypass traditional, centralized DOI infrastructures, the identifier scheme generates permanent, cryptographically tied addresses for academic and literary works. [[1], [2], [3], [4]] The Structure of an AXN An AXN identifier is constructed in three distinct layers using the following format: `AXN:<HEX>.<FAMILY>.<6 EMOJI>` [1] * `<HEX>` (Positional Anchor): A 4-digit hexadecimal label corresponding to the canonical deposit number (e.g., `AXN:0379`). * `<FAMILY>` (Semantic Category): A keyword defining the category of the work (e.g., `EMPIRICAL`, `GENERATIVE`), auto-detected from keywords or manually assigned. * `<6 EMOJI>` (Content Hash): A visual cryptographic hash functioning as an immutable link to the specific text. It represents the first 6 bytes of the SHA-256 hash of the deposit's canonical bytes, translated into a 6-emoji sequence (e.g., `⚙️🏛️⚡🔑...`). [[1], [2], [3]] Why It's Used Alexanarch created the AXN protocol in response to the fragility of traditional metadata registries (like DataCite/Zenodo), which have experienced issues with records and metadata being silently removed. Because the identifier's visual hash is mathematically derived directly from the content itself, it ensures the document remains citable, discoverable, and attributable without needing a centralized registrar. [[1], [2], [3], [4], [5]] You can explore the registry and read the full identifier protocol on the [Alexanarch Identifiers Documentation](https://www.alexanarch.org/identifiers/) or browse the [Alexanarch Home Repository](https://www.alexanarch.org/). [1] Would you like to know more about how to deposit a work to receive an AXN identifier, or are you looking for details on the JSON-LD metadata tied to these records?
